# X5 — normal/roughness/AO arrays for the cross-LB statics atlas (`?statNra`)

**Date:** 2026-07-28/29 · **Plan:** `docs/terrainplan.md` §2 X5 · **Handoff:** `docs/HANDOFF-xtrack-statics-textures-2026-07-28.md` §2
**Status:** implemented, **DEFAULT-OFF** behind `?statNra=on`, local SwiftShader validation done, **not committed** (left for review).
**Touched:** `apps/holtburger-web/scene3d/static_atlas.js`, `apps/holtburger-web/docs/url-flags.md`, this file.

---

## 1. The gap X5 closes

`scene3d/static_atlas.js` was **albedo-only v1**: the cross-LB bucket material replaced each member's
material with a `MeshStandardMaterial` whose `map` is a `sampler2DArray`, and everything else the member
carried was dropped. The header said so ("v1 drops it for the atlased path -> slightly flatter shading, an
eye-test trade"), and after the 2026-07-28 smear fix (`1ed8a067`) the 1070 confirmed the residual delta on
real hardware: default vs `?statAtlas=off` now match **except** that atlased buildings read flat-roofed.

The atlas also flattened `roughness` to a constant 1.0, which is why atlased statics could not pick up the
T3 sky-IBL env specular the terrain got in `73d7e31b` (three drives env reflection sharpness and strength
off `roughnessFactor`).

## 2. What the singleton path actually has — measured, not assumed

Live census, `?statAtlas=off&quality=high`, Holtburg, walking the real `staticsGroup` and de-duplicating by
material uuid (`scratchpad/singleton-probe.mjs`):

| sample | unique materials | `map` | `normalMap` | `roughnessMap` | `aoMap` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t+6 s | 51 | 51 | **51** | 0 | 0 |
| t+42 s | 90 | 90 | **68** | 0 | 0 |
| t+54 s | 123 | 123 | **80** | 0 | 0 |

Every lit `MeshStandardMaterial` carries a `normalMap`; the shortfall in the later rows is exactly the
non-standard materials that also report `roughness === undefined` (unlit/particle billboards, which the
atlas never consumes anyway). So:

* **normalMap — universal.** Source: `adapter.js surfacePixelsToNormalTexture`, an RGBA8 `DataTexture`
  padded from the wasm `holtburger_dat::normal_gen::normal_from_luminance` RGB8 (a Sobel-from-luminance
  *derived* normal — retail has no normal maps; nothing is invented here, and nothing new is generated by
  X5 either). `NoColorSpace`, same dimensions as the albedo (both go through the same `downscaleRgba`).
* **`normalScale` varies per material** and is the per-category table
  (`materials.js CATEGORY_NORMAL_SCALE_DEFAULTS`): measured distribution `1.00`×10 (Stone), `0.80`×17
  (default), `0.70`×29 (Wood), `0.50`×21 (Foliage/Cloth), `0.40`×2, `0.30`×1.
* **`roughness` scalar varies per material**: `0.80`×29, `0.85`×31, `0.90`×18, `0.95`×2 — the atlas was
  flattening all of these to 1.0.
* **`metalness` is 0.00 on every measured material** at Holtburg.
* **`roughnessMap` / `aoMap`: ZERO, on the singleton path too.** The Phase-5 texchan bake
  (`materials.js _applyRough`, fed by `dist/suite/texchan-manifest.json`, which serves 200) resolved only
  **4** `.texchan.bin` fetches in a whole session. So these two channels are plumbed but currently carry
  nothing on either path — X5 is at parity, not behind it.

## 3. Array layout

One parallel `DataArrayTexture` per bucket, same `w`/`h`/capacity as the diffuse array, so the existing
per-vertex `aLayer` attribute and the single `vMapUv` address **both** arrays. Packed exactly like the
terrain T2 "nra" array (`adapter.js buildPbrNraTexture`, `terrain.js pbrN`):

| channel | content | source |
|---|---|---|
| R | tangent-normal **X**, `normalScale` baked in | `material.normalMap.r` |
| G | tangent-normal **Y**, `normalScale` baked in | `material.normalMap.g` |
| B | roughness | `material.roughness × roughnessMap.g` (roughnessMap absent → the scalar alone) |
| A | ambient occlusion | `material.aoMap.r` (absent → 255 = unoccluded) |

Normal **Z is reconstructed in-shader** on the unit hemisphere
(`sqrt(max(1 - dot(xy,xy), 0.04))`) — terrain's convention, adopted for consistency. `NoColorSpace`,
`ClampToEdge` + the shader's `fract()` for wrap buckets (identical addressing contract to the diffuse
array — they must agree or relief would slide off its albedo on tiling surfaces).

Unwritten / recycled layers read the **flat texel `(128,128,255,255)`** = flat normal, roughness
multiplier 1.0, no occlusion — i.e. byte-identical shading to albedo-only v1. `packNraLayer` always writes
all four channels for the whole layer, so a recycled layer can never bleed its previous surface's relief.

**Why `normalScale` is baked into XY rather than passed as a uniform:** three does `mapN.xy *= normalScale`
before normalizing, so folding it in at pack time is the same math — and it avoids a per-layer uniform
array, keeping `customProgramCacheKey` **per-bucket-class, never per-instance** (the project's #1
cold-load-cost invariant). Layer dedup keys on the diffuse texture uuid, and the same texture means the
same DID means the same category means the same scale, so the first-writer choice carries no drift.

### Shader wiring

`onBeforeCompile` swaps four `#include` directives (directive-level, before three resolves includes — the
2026-07-02 white-trees lesson):

1. `<map_fragment>` — assigns the shared global `_statNraTexel` (one array sample, reused by the three
   sites below, all in `main()` scope), then the unchanged diffuse multiply.
2. `<roughnessmap_fragment>` — `float roughnessFactor = roughness * _statNraTexel.b;`. The bucket material
   keeps `roughness = 1.0`, so the multiply reproduces the member's value exactly. **This is the line that
   feeds the T3 env specular.**
3. `<normal_fragment_maps>` — decode XY, reconstruct Z, `normal = normalize(tbn * mapN)`. `tbn` is the
   stock derivative frame from `<normal_fragment_begin>`; to get three to emit it, the bucket material is
   given the same **1×1 white dummy** as `normalMap` that the file already uses for `map` (it forces
   `USE_NORMALMAP_TANGENTSPACE`; it is never sampled).
4. `<aomap_fragment>` — `(_statNraTexel.a - 1) * 0.6 + 1` (the singleton path's `aoMapIntensity`), applied
   to `indirectDiffuse`, plus three's own `computeSpecularOcclusion` branch under
   `#if defined(USE_ENVMAP) && defined(STANDARD)`.

`customProgramCacheKey` gains an `nra` suffix: `statAtlasArrayMatV3w|c` → `…nra`. Two variants become four,
still per-bucket-class. **No light-count change anywhere.**

### Late-arriving roughness/AO

`materials.js _resolveRough` attaches `roughnessMap`/`aoMap` **asynchronously** (HTTP fetch of a per-DID
`.texchan.bin` + wasm decode), routinely after the atlas has already consumed the surface. Layers packed
without them are queued in `_nraPending` and re-packed from the existing ~10 Hz PVS tick
(`tickStatAtlasOptimize`) once both maps land. The first cut used a 6 s budget and **every** entry expired
unfed; it is now 60 s. Entries whose layer has since been recycled to a different surface are dropped, never
re-written. The list is empty and never appended to with the flag off.

## 4. Unique-surface count before/after dedup (X5 deliverable)

Instrumented into the existing `window.__atlasStats()` surface, plus a one-line `console.info` per feed
(dev flag only — never on the default path):

* `surfaceRefs` — every atlas-able member's surface reference (**before** dedup)
* `uniqueSurfacesEver` — distinct surface textures ever atlased (`_uniqueTexUuids`)
* `liveLayers` — layers resident right now (sum of per-bucket `layerOf.size`)
* `layerAllocs` / `layerHits` / `layerRecycles` — cuts, refcount reuse, recycled-after-eviction
* `dedupRatio` = `surfaceRefs / uniqueSurfacesEver`

Measured at Holtburg (`quality=high&atlasTilePx=512`, both arms):

| arm | feeds | atlased | **surfaceRefs (pre-dedup)** | **uniqueSurfaces (post-dedup)** | liveLayers | dedupRatio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (flag absent) | 1 | 65 | 65 | 28 | 28 | 2.32 |
| default (flag absent) | 9 | 112 | 112 | 54 | 54 | 2.07 |
| `?statNra=on` | 26 | 156 | 156 | **59** | 59 | **2.64** |

So the atlas packs ~2.1–2.6 member surfaces per texture layer; the nra array costs exactly the
**post-dedup** count (59 layers), not the pre-dedup one (156). Per-bucket rows (`w`,`h`,`stateKey`,
`capacity`, `layersUsed`, `nra`) are in `__atlasStats().buckets`.

## 5. Validation (local, SwiftShader, no GPU)

**Offline, against the real three r184 `ShaderLib.physical`** (node harness driving the actual module):

* **Flag ABSENT is byte-identical to HEAD `1ed8a067`** for both bucket variants — fragment source, vertex
  source, uniform set, `customProgramCacheKey`, `normalMap` (unset), `roughness`, and layer capacity all
  compare equal against the HEAD file loaded side-by-side in the same process. Re-verified after every
  subsequent edit.
* With the flag on: all four `#include` directives are actually replaced (no leftovers), `uNraArray` is
  declared and bound, `tbn` is used, cache key is `…nra`.
* Pack math is exact: for `normalMap` byte 200/60 at `normalScale` 0.5, `roughness` 0.85 with
  `roughnessMap.g` 204, and an AO map at a **different tile size** (exercising the nearest-neighbour
  resampler), the packed layer is `(164, 94, 173, 100)` — matching the hand-computed expectation — and an
  untouched layer stays `(128,128,255,255)`.

**Live boots** (`http://127.0.0.1:8765/…?nosw=1&quality=high&atlasTilePx=512&autoLogin=1&autoSpawn=first&kickDance=1&agent=1`,
`@god` + `@telepoi Holtburg`, ~135 s settle):

| | default (flag absent) | `?statNra=on` |
|---|---|---|
| bootState | **in-world** | **in-world** |
| console errors / pageerrors | **0** | **0** |
| buckets | 15 | 16, **all 16 with an nra array** |
| statAtlas programs linked | `statAtlasArrayMatV3w` | **`statAtlasArrayMatV3wnra`** |
| layers packed | — | **59 / 59** |
| layers with a real normal map | — | **59** (100%) |
| layers with roughnessMap / aoMap | — | 0 / 0 (see §2 — absent on both paths) |
| peak sampled chrome RSS | 5,818 MB | 6,316 MB |

No shader-compile or link errors in either arm (three throws a console error on a failed program; the only
`shader`-matching console lines are the normal `renderer.compile` / `rig warm` info logs).

**Memory — a real trap, found and fixed.** The first cut kept the per-bucket layer capacity unchanged
"for A/B parity". That doubled per-bucket texture bytes and **earlyoom SIGTERM'd the renderer at 5,164 MiB
RSS** (SwiftShader keeps every texture in system RAM; ~14 live buckets went from ~175 MB of array bytes to
~350 MB, ×~1.33 for mips, ×2 for the driver copy). Fixed by making the two arrays **share** the byte
budget: `_layerCapacityFor` counts both arrays per layer and the ceiling/floor halve
(`_ATLAS_NRA_MAX_LAYERS` 128, `_ATLAS_NRA_MIN_LAYERS` 16). Observed capacities drop 256/128/32 → 128/64/16
while live usage is 28–59 layers, so nothing overflows (`ptLayerFull = 0` in every run) and overflow is
fail-soft anyway. After the fix the `=on` arm completes a full Holtburg session; note the **default** arm
also peaks at 5.8 GB on this 8 GB box, so the two arms sit in the same band and the two crashes seen along
the way are this laptop's ceiling, not an nra-specific regression. This wants a clean re-measure on a box
that is not memory-starved.

## 6. What remains before this can flip default-ON

1. **Real-GPU 1070 eyetest** — per project rules; batched with the next 1070 session (another session owns
   this; not attempted here). What to look for: atlased buildings gaining roof/wall relief and matching
   `?statAtlas=off`; no seam sparkle at wrap-bucket tile repeats (the nra array shares the diffuse array's
   half-texel wrap-seam trade); no over-bright env specular now that roughness is 0.80–0.95 instead of 1.0.
2. **Bare-default bar** — already met on SwiftShader for the flag-off path (loads, spawns, 0 errors, and
   byte-identical to HEAD). The `=on` path meets it too locally; it needs the same on real hardware.
3. **A look call on reconstructed-Z.** Terrain reconstructs Z from XY; three's stock path keeps the stored
   Z and scales XY. At a given `normalScale` the two differ slightly in tilt. Consistency with terrain won;
   worth one eyetest glance.
4. **Memory re-measure on a non-starved box** (see §5) to confirm the shared-budget capacities are right
   rather than merely survivable, and to decide whether the halved ceiling should also apply when a real
   GPU has VRAM to spare.

## 7. Risks / limitations

* **`metalness` is not carried** — no free channel in the nra pack (A is AO, per the terrain convention).
  Every atlas bucket has always rendered metalness 0, and 100% of measured Holtburg statics are 0.00, so
  this changes nothing today; a Metal-category surface (0.9) inside an atlas bucket would still read
  non-metal. Would need a 5th channel or a second array.
* **Roughness/AO are dead weight until the texchan bake covers more DIDs** (§2). The machinery is in and
  costs nothing (`_nraPending` holds tens of entries for ≤60 s); the visible win today is the normal map
  plus the per-material roughness scalar replacing the flat 1.0.
* **First-writer wins per layer.** Layer dedup keys on the diffuse texture uuid, so if two materials ever
  shared one albedo texture with different `normalScale`/`roughness`, the first would win. Same texture ⇒
  same DID ⇒ same category ⇒ same values, so this is believed unreachable; `__atlasStats()` would not
  currently show it if it happened.
* **VRAM.** Even with the shared budget, a bucket now holds two arrays; on a GPU the total bytes are
  ~unchanged but the count of texture objects and the mip chains double.
* **Not applied to the legacy per-(LB,size) merge path** `consolidateSingletonsViaTexArray`, which has no
  callers (the cross-LB path superseded it). It stays albedo-only v1.
